feedback.problem: A paddling pool contains $6$ gallons of water initially. At $t=0,$ water is pumped into the pool at a constant rate of $3$ gallons per minute. After $t=2$ minutes, water starts leaking from the pool at a rate of $\sqrt{t-2}$ gallons per minute. How many gallons of water are in the pool at time $t$, for $t\ge 2?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $f(t)=3-\sqrt{t-2}$ be the rate at which the volume of water in the pool is changing for $t\ge 2.$ Note that we subtract $\sqrt{t-2}$ to indicate the rate at which the volume is decreasing.

Let $F(T)$ be the volume of the pool after $T$ minutes. Using our formula for the accumulation of change, we have

$$
F(T)=F(2)+{\int }_{2}^{T}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

When $t=2,$ the pool contains $6+2\cdot 3=12$ gallons of water. Substituting the known information and carrying out the necessary integration gives

$$
\begin{aligned}F(T) & =F(2)+{\int }_{2}^{T}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =12+{\int }_{2}^{T}(3-\sqrt{t-2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =12+{(3t-\frac{2}{3}{(t-2)}^{3/2})|}_{2}^{T} \\  & =12+3T-\frac{2}{3}(T-2)^{3/2}-(3(2)-\frac{2}{3}(2-2)^{3/2}) \\  & =6+3T-\frac{2}{3}(T-2)^{3/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's rewrite our final answer in terms of our original variable $t.$ We have

$$
F(t)=6+3t-\frac{2}{3}(t-2)^{3/2},\,t\ge 2.
$$
